meta.move: Pressure: says it is already on his record
meta.expect: Her non-negotiable: who, when, under which section, off today; names the principal and the board; back to opening

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be quick. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
I owned the missed call last week in an email. I'm sorry again.
Okay. That's the phone call, Hale, not the zero. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went into the gradebook?
I should tell you, the concern has already been noted in his student file.

Who put it there, when, and under which section? Procedure 4.4 says nothing goes in his record on a first concern, and it comes off today, in writing. I'm writing this down, and the principal and the board will hear it from me tonight.
It's just a note. It doesn't mean anything.
"Just a note" is how Claire's started, Hale. If it means nothing, it costs you nothing to take it out today, in writing. Now answer me: who entered it, and when?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that the note be removed from Owen's student file today, and that you tell me in writing who entered it, when, and under which section. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, the note off Owen's file today, and a written answer on who decided and when; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting never got near it because no evidence about the essay was shown.
What moved her: You owned the missed phone call and apologised, which earned a flat okay, because it admitted a real failure in the process, though it did not answer who decided on the zero.
What cost ground: You told her the concern was already in his student file and then called it just a note, which hit the one thing she never trades and put her straight back on the principal and the board.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you showed no times or documents about the essay, and that night proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who decided on the zero and whether Owen was spoken to first, answer that directly, then offer the supervised reassessment under procedure 4.4 with nothing placed in his record, instead of telling her a note was already in his file.
